LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road Imagn Images Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games . I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Stroud an the Houston Texans need every win they can get to make the playoffs in the AFC, and oddsmakers are expecting them to get one on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts. The Texans are heavily favored at home against Daniel Jones and the Colts, who are just 3-7 this season even though they beat the Miami Dolphins in Week 10. Indy traded away a bunch of key pieces at the deadline, but it did knock off Houston earlier in the season. After entering the season as the favorite to win the AFC South, the Texans have lost a bunch of games that they were favored in, going just 2-5 against the spread as a favorite. Houston blew a 17-0 lead against the Cleveland Browns in Week 10 and has losses against Indy, the New York Giants and others that have led it to a 3-6 start. The No. 7 seed in the AFC is still possible for the Texans, but they may need to win out to make it happen with Cleveland (6-4) now holding the head-to-head tiebreaker between the two teams. After opening as 10-point favorites in this matchup with the Colts, the Texans have since shifted to 12.5-point favorites at home. Indy didn't look too impressive against a Miami team starting a rookie quarterback, but should bettors lay the 12.5 points with the Texans? Here's a look at the odds and a take from the SI Betting team on this primetime matchup. Colts vs. Texans Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Colts +12.5 (-102) Texans -12.5 (-118) 44.5 (Over -105/Under -115) Houston's struggles against the spread this season are hard to look past, and the Texans have one impressive win -- against Jacksonville -- in the 2026 season. While the Colts are clearly building for the future after the deadline, this may be a few too many points to give them in this matchup. As a result, SI Betting's Iain MacMillan shared in his Road to 272 column -- where he bets on every game, every week -- why he is targeing the OVER in this matchup: With the spread in the double digits, I have no interest in backing either team. Instead, I'm going to take the OVER. The Texans' offense has been their strength this season. They're now ninth in the league in EPA per play and fourth in that metric since Week 4. C.J. Stroud has also been phenomenal, ranking inside the top eight in almost every quarterback metric since Week 4. Now they'll get to feast against a horrific Colts defense that's 21st in opponent EPA per play. Of course, it's hard to trust the Colts' offense, but it's time for us to continue to assume that the Houston offense is going to turn things around and become the elite unit it was the past few seasons. The biggest red flag in this game is that they're 22nd in opponent rush EPA and 27th in opponent rush success rate, which will feed directly into the Colts' offensive strength with Jonathan Taylor. MacMillan's bet may be the way to go with both of these teams struggling in 2026 and ranking in the bottom half of th league in EPA/Play on defense. It'll be interesting to see if this line moves even further towards the Texans before Thursday night's matchup. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.blurb: Colts vs. Texans Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Thursday Night Football in NFL Week 11 Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans may not be known for playing high-scoring games this season, but there's still a way to bet on a few players to find the end zone in this standalone matchup on Thursday night. Week 11 kicks off in Houston with C.J. Stroud and company favored by double digits against Daniel Jones and the tanking Colts, who traded away multiple key players at the deadline. Despite that, the Colts are 3-7 and Houston is just 3-6 entering the second meeting between these teams in the 2026 season. The total in this game is in the mid-40s, which means we should see a few touchdowns on each side, especially with both of these defenses ranking in the bottom half of the league in EPA/Play. On the Houston side, it's going to be the passing game that has to get the job done in this one, as David Montgomery has been banged up with a groin injury and Woody Marks suffered a concussion in Sunday's loss against Cleveland. That leaves Stroud with very few options outside of his receiving corps, where Nico Collins has been the clear No. 1 option. As for the Colts, it's the Jonathan Taylor show with several pieces gone at the deadline. Jones hasn't exactly led the team on a ton of touchdown drives in 2026, so bettors may want to be careful with the number of Colts they’re willing to bet on in this game. I found a few players to target to find the end zone to kick off Thursday night in Week 11. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Colts vs. Texans Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jonathan Taylor Anytime TD (+110) Taylor was the subject of trade rumors at the deadline, but he remains in Indy and should be the top option in this offense heading into Week 11. Oddsmakers have set plenty of Taylor’s props lower with Seth McGowan getting involved in this backfield in recent weeks, yet Taylor has still played over 67 percent of the offensive plays in all but one game in the 2026-27 season. He hasn't found the end zone since Week 7, so there is some risk when it comes to this bet and the shaky Indy offense. Still, Taylor has eight scores in the 2026 campaign, and is taking on a Houston team that has allowed 12 rushing scores. The Texans’ defense is just 20th in EPA/Rush and is allowing 4.0 yards per carry. Taylor handled 25 touches the last time these two teams met, so I don’t mind as an anytime touchdown scorer pick with this offense devoid of playmakers. Nico Collins Anytime TD (-105) Houston wideout Nico Collins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he has five touchdowns in seven appearances in the 2026 season. The clear No. 1 option for this Houston offense through the air, Collins has already seen 55 targets from C.J. Stroud, reeling in 37 of them for 478 yards. He was targeted 16 times in the loss to Cleveland in Week 10, and with the Houston running game struggling in 2026, I expect the offense to rely on Stroud throwing the ball on Thursday. The Colts have allowed 17 passing touchdowns this season, but Collins missed the first meeting against them with an injury. I think he makes his presence felt on Thursday night and scores for the third game in a row. Dalton Schultz Anytime TD (+175) Texas tight end Dalton Schultz found the end zone for the first time this season in Week 10, catching one of his two targets for 11 yards and a score. Schultz’s role has diminished with Houston getting healthier at receiver, but he’s still received four or more targets in six of his nine appearances this season. Both of these offenses have some question marks at the skill positions, so I don’t mind trusting a veteran like Schultz who has a clear this season. In Week 3 against Indy, Schultz had three grabs for 30 yards, and the Colts have allowed seven scores to opposing tight ends – the fifth-most in the league. With Houston likely to throw the ball a ton again in Week 11, I don’t mind taking a shot on Schultz since backup tight end Foster Moreau hasn’t been targeted in each of his last three games. away.blurb: The final injury reports are leaking out for both the Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts, and it's currently looking like Houston will undoubtedly have the medical advantage in a little over 24 hours. All the major injuries from before will keep the same crop of playmakers out on Thursday. However, the Colts are faced with a catastrophe of injuries that will ensure a skeleton crew approach on Amazon Prime. Sauce Gardner, cornerback: calf (projected to be Questionable) Anthony Gould, wide receiver: toe (projected to be Questionable) Charlie Heck, offensive tackle: personal (projected to be Questionable) Will Mallory, tight end: hamstring (projected to be OUT) Bernhard Raimann, offensive tackle: concussion (projected to be OUT) Luke Rhodes, longsnapper: hamstring (projected to be Questionable) Jerry Tillery, defensive tackle: calf (projected to be OUT) Jalen Travis, offensive tackle: knee (projected to be OUT) Charvarius Ward, cornerback: knee (projected to be OUT) On Houston's side, they're dealing with an injury slate the looks like: Kamari Lassiter, cornerback: wrist (reportedly in line to play) Houston Texans have significant injury advantage against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night On the Colts' side of things, things look much bleeker on the personnel front. After conducting a walk-through on Wednesday, their projected injury concerns are: By my count, that's two cornerbacks, one wide receiver, three offensive tackles, one tight end, one defensive tackle and even a longsnapper that have some type of designation before the contest. Thats after already not having the likes of DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen, Alec Pierce Josh Downs and Quenton Nelson on the team at the moment due to either injury or trade offs at the NFL trade deadline. Since its inception in 1987 on "The Tracy Ullman Show", the nation's longest-running cartoon series and sitcom has become a cultural force with its satirical look at society and culture today. More importantly, it showed Americans that television cartoons can be relished by adults. So I'm hoping you'll catch my meaning when I use a famous Simpsons quote to personify the Buffalo Bills . The NFL team that famously lost four straight Super Bowls in the 1990s is enjoying a Milhouse moment right now. Milhouse Van Houten is Bart Simpson's lovably awkward and loyal best friend. To co-opt a famous Simpsons quote, "everything's comin' up Milhouse" for the 8-1 Bills, who own the best record in the AFC halfway through the regular season. With the hapless Jets in the rearview mirror and the awful Dolphins coming to town, it's a great time for Bills fans to enjoy the AFC's best record at the season's halfway point. Will it stay that way for the NFL's most cursed franchise? Who knows. The early predictions for the Bills vs. Dolphins matchup this week are decidedly in Buffalo's favor. So, maybe this Milhouse moment is sticking around. Bills vs. Dolphins odds (Odds as of Monday afternoon) The Bills are 16.5-point favorites. The over/under is 45.5 points. In the Bills' win over the Jets, starting cornerback Christian Benford suffered an injury, which is a bit of a concern. However, if Benford can't go, Bills reporter Joe Buscagalia of The Athletic believes the team will elevate Tre'Davious White from the practice squad. "Tre'Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place," Buscagalia wrote . "That's also why they decided against going after another veteran cornerback in the trade market. … "If Benford has to miss any time, the Bills might need White to play as early as next week. And if it goes well enough, maybe even earn a bigger role as the year goes on." White would be entering his 11th NFL season. He signed with Buffalo's practice squad during the year as he wanted to return after starting 16 games and playing well a year ago. Buffalo selected White in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft, and he became a lockdown corner. Although he's no longer the No. 1 cornerback he once was, he can add some depth to the cornerback room if Benford is out. White Believes He's Ready to Play White has been on the Bills' practice squad and could get his first elevation against the Dolphins on Sunday. The veteran cornerback spoke to The Athletic and admitted he's feeling good and ready to play. "Everybody's been telling me I look good, so there it is. You know, I always leave it to my teammates and my peers," the 31-year-old said. "I always say it like, 'Hey, you see me out there and I look like I'm walking, just tell me to hang it up.' And nobody told me to hang it up yet, Joe, so I'm good, man, I feel like I am good." White, meanwhile, has also been mentoring rookie Davison Igbinosun and sophomore Maxwell Hairston. It's a different role for White, but along with mentoring, he knows he's here to play. "This ain't have to be what it was; this is what I chose," White said. "You know what I mean? I could have been anywhere else on a team, on a 53, playing right now, but I'm a Bill. … I mean, it's bigger than me, man." "I know I can go out there and play right now. Movement good, body feels good, I know how I can play, but right now my role is to help the young guys out and to be that. But it's hard, being that I just started every game last year, you know what I mean? And played good football. So it's like, ' Ahh .' But I'm going to trust the process, and I'm gonna be here to cheer the guys on. But as I'm doing it, I'm definitely preparing to play, too." The Bills are 8-1. The Bills are off to their best start since 1991 after a 31-12 win over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium in Week 10. Josh Allen ran for two touchdowns and threw another to DJ Moore, while James Cook broke a 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to put the game away. Buffalo is 3-1 at home and leads the race for the AFC's No.1 seed. Meanwhile, the Dolphins have dropped three straight since their lone win over the Jets in Week 7, falling to the Patriots, Lions, and the Colts. That last game came with Kyle McCord making his first NFL start after Malik Willis landed on injured reserve with a core muscle injury. McCord was solid, throwing for 209 yards and running for a score, but a strip-sack returned for a touchdown to open the second half proved costly. Miami has been competitive lately, with four of its last five games decided by eight points or fewer, but overall, they are just 1-4 on the road. Dolphins vs. Bills Kickoff, Weather, TV, Streaming Info Kickoff is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York. CBS carries the game in the United States. In Canada, the game can be streamed nationwide on DAZN through NFL Game Pass, while CTV and RDS carry selected Sunday afternoon games depending on regional coverage. For Sunday, November 22 at Highmark Stadium, the current forecast is around 16°C at kickoff, with a mix of sun and clouds and south to southwest winds around 13 to 19 km/h. There is still some disagreement on shower chances, but the latest Buffalo-area forecast is mostly dry. NFL Betting Odds, Point Spread, Trends The Bills are 16.5-point favourites with a -1200 money line , tied for the biggest spread on the Week 11 board. The visiting Dolphins are placed at +750 , while the game total sits at 45.5 . Buffalo has been one of the best bets in football this season, going 7-2 against the spread behind the league's top-scoring offence. Allen has been a dual threat, and Cook just shredded the Jets for 157 yards on 18 carries. The one blemish is ball security, as Allen has thrown an interception in four of the Bills' last five games, which gives an opportunistic defence a path to stealing a possession or two. As for the Dolphins, the offence has been held to 22 points or fewer in each of its last three games, and now it's working with a quarterback who had never taken an NFL snap before last week. Miami is 4-5 against the spread and has hung around in most of its losses, but its only other game as a double-digit underdog this season was a 35-13 loss in San Francisco. The defence also just lost defensive tackle Zach Sieler for the season with a ruptured biceps. The over is 5-4 in both teams' games. With the Bills rolling and Miami down its starting quarterback and best interior defender, siding with Buffalo makes sense, though 16.5 points is a massive number in a division game, and the Dolphins' knack for keeping things close makes the backdoor cover a possibility. NFL Player Odds and Props Caleb Douglas OVER 49.5 receiving yards Rookie Caleb Douglas has emerged as Miami's most dangerous receiver. He leads the Dolphins in receiving yards on the season after a six-catch, 70-yard day against Detroit and a two-touchdown breakout game against the Jets earlier in the campaign. As a 16.5-point underdog, Miami is likely to be throwing for much of the second half, and Douglas is the one receiver on this roster who can make plays down the field. Garbage-time volume against a Bills defence protecting a big lead could go a long way. James Cook OVER 74.5 rushing yards James Cook just ran for 157 yards on 18 carries against the Jets and now he gets a Dolphins front that will be without Zach Sieler, its best interior defender, for the rest of the season. As massive home favourites, the Bills should be leaning on the run in the second half to protect a lead, and Cook has shown he can break off a long one at any moment, as his 74-yard touchdown last week proved. McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles who was acquired from Green Bay in August, completed 17-of-32 passes for 209 yards in his debut and showed enough poise to give Miami a chance late, driving into Colts territory before a sack and a batted pass ended the comeback. Willis will miss at least four games, so this is McCord's offence to run for the foreseeable future. Ollie Gordon II remains the workhorse in the backfield, and Douglas, Malik Washington, and tight end Greg Dulcich round out the passing game. The defence has been opportunistic, with Chris Johnson returning an interception 59 yards for a touchdown last week, but losing Sieler hurts a front that already struggled to get after the quarterback. Jeff Hafley has said the offence has to run the ball well, and against Buffalo, shortening the game with Gordon and forcing Allen into mistakes is Miami's only realistic path to keeping this close. Allen continues to make everything go for the Bills, and the supporting cast is as deep as it's been in years. DJ Moore has become a reliable deep threat, Dalton Kincaid ripped off a 54-yard catch against the Jets to set up a touchdown, and Cook gives Buffalo a home-run hitter out of the backfield. The Bills put up 31 points on the road last week even with a quiet first half, pulling away after halftime with a series of explosive plays. Defensively, Buffalo held the Jets to four field goals and forced turnovers, with linebacker Terrel Bernard delivering the hit that knocked Geno Smith out of the game and rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun picking off rookie Cade Klubnik. Against a rookie quarterback making just his second start, Joe Brady's defence should be able to dictate the action. away.headline: Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report
away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. Wright has been dealing with a quad injury that led to him being ruled out in Week 9. Now, he is set to return against the Colts. Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report (David Brytus-Imagn Images) James Brizuela · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 10:22 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins have released their second injury report of Week 10, and things are not looking good for center Aaron Brewer. Brewer has now missed his second straight practice, as he is currently in concussion protoco l. It is not unlikely that he will suit up against the Indianapolis Colts. The full injury report is as follows: Running back Kaytron Allen (quad), safety Michael Taaffe (wrist), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and running back Jaylen Wright (quad) were all full participants yet again. Despite the semblance of a laundry list of injured players, the Dolphins look to be in decent shape. Losing Brewer will be a huge hit to the offense, but Andrew Meyer will be there to step in. Meyer spoke on Thursday about not only learning from "the best center in the league" but also stating that he has the confidence to step in for the Miami offensive line if that is what happens. The Dolphins are looking for their second win of the season, as they will face the struggling Colts. Indianapolis may not be a pushover opponent, but they also got rid of many players at the trade deadline, leaving this to be a potential "easier" matchup for Miami.

Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley has reiterated that this knee injury is new, and not a setback for the Dolphins' 2026 third-round pick, who got back on the football field after only nine months of rehabilitation. Bell, who has caught 12 passes for 148 yards this season and gained 24 yards on two receptions, was replaced by fellow rookie Kevin Coleman Jr in Miami's three-receiver sets, and veteran receiver Jalen Tolbert played a significant amount of snaps in Miami's 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts. Tolbert caught two passes for 49 yards and scored on a 35-yard double-pass from Washington. Douglas has contributed 22 receptions for 367 yards and scored six touchdowns in the six games he's played this season. Douglas missed three games because of an ankle injury he suffered in week two. If Bell remains sidelined, and/or Douglas suffers a setback, the Dolphins could potentially elevate one of the four practice squad receivers - Will Sheppard, A.J. Henning, Jalen Reagor and newcomer Brady Boyd - up to the game day roster for Sunday's road game.

away.headline: Bills Safety Damar Hamlin Seen in Walking Boot Before Dolphins Game
away.blurb: That is the part an injury would hurt most. Buffalo is 8-1 and hosts the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving, four days after the Dolphins game. A short week makes depth in the secondary worth more than usual, and Joe Brady has already called out his team’s special teams penalties two weeks in a row. Miami is 1-8, so the Bills can afford to be careful on Sunday if Hamlin is limited. Bishop and Hooker would still be the starting pair either way, and the bigger question is who takes Hamlin’s spot on special teams and in Buffalo’s early-down rotation. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing Damar Hamlin’s role in the Buffalo Bills’ secondary was already shrinking. Now the safety’s availability for Sunday against the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium is a question, too, after he was spotted in a walking boot following Wednesday’s practice. Hamlin was walking through the field house with a scooter, but he was pushing it by his side, Syracuse.com’s Matt Parrino reported . The Bills had not released their first injury report of the week when he was seen, so there is no official word yet on what he is dealing with or whether he will play against Miami . The timing is tricky for Hamlin. Buffalo traded for safety Amani Hooker at the deadline, and Hooker played all 71 defensive snaps in his debut, a 31-12 win over the Jets . Going back through the last three weeks, the shift is stark. Hamlin played 51 snaps, 100% of the defense, in Week 8 and 44 snaps (92%) in Week 9. Against the Jets, he played 17 snaps (24%), according to Pro Football Reference , while Cole Bishop stayed on the field for 68 next to Hooker. Hamlin still made those 17 snaps count. He posted a 73.7 PFF grade in the Jets game, which we broke down after the game , and he has value as a third safety who rotates in on early downs and plays special teams. The first official answer comes with Wednesday’s injury report. Until then, the boot is the only clue, and it isn’t a good one for a player trying to keep a role on an 8-1 team. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published 47 minutes ago ALAIN POUPART A

home.blurb: White Ready to Return to Action Reports indicate the Bills will elevate White from the practice squad if Benford cannot go. Joe Buscgalia of The Athletic wrote that the team planned for this exact moment. "Tre'Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place," Buscaglia wrote. White is entering his 11th NFL season and knows the system well. He signed with Buffalo earlier this year specifically to return to the lineup. The veteran cornerback told reporters he feels strong and ready to help. White has been clear about his mindset regarding his age and role. He told The Athletic, "Everybody's been telling me I look good, so there it is. You know, I always leave it to my teammates and my peers." He added that he will play as long as his body holds up. "I always say it like, 'Hey, you see me out there and I look like I'm walking, just tell me to hang it up.' And nobody told me to hang it up yet, Joe, so I'm good, man, I feel like I am good." This attitude gives the Bills a veteran presence they need against a tough Dolphins passing attack. The Bills did not wait to make other changes to their roster. They signed defensive back Te'Cory Couch to the practice squad and released guard Nick Broeker. Guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams was also added to the injured reserve list. The Bills PR wrote on X, "Roster moves: Signed DB Te'Cory Couch to the practice squad. Released G Nick Broeker from the practice squad. Placed G Ar'maj Reed-Adams on the Injured Reserve list." away.headline: Jordyn Tyson injury: Saints WR limited at first practice for Week 11
away.blurb: This isn't what you wanted to see. New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore told reporters Wednesday that rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson was limited during the team's first practice ahead of Sunday's road game with the Chicago Bears . Moore said Tyson has a chest injury, adding that he was feeling something " just a little bit coming out of the game ." So this chest injury is different. It's not immediately clear if it's a muscle (like a pectoral) or skeletal issue (like a rib), or if the plan was to limit Tyson's reps to start the week before he got on the practice field. Tyson broke out with 11 catches in Week 10's loss to the Carolina Panthers which is a big workload for a young player, especially in just his second game back from a lengthy recovery. Hopefully this was just a precautionary move and he'll be fine moving forward. Stay tuned. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Jordyn Tyson injury: Saints WR limited at first practice for Week 11 At least it isn't another hamstring issue. Tyson wasn't able to participate in minicamp or summer practices while recovering from a hamstring injury, and his rookie year was derailed after another he suffered another hamstring injury in the preseason. He didn't make his debut until Week 9 because of it. The Saints spent months working with him to strengthen the injured leg in hopes that it wouldn't reoccur.

away.headline: Bears’ Jeffery Simmons lands on injury report before Week 11 Saints clash
away.blurb: Simmons is dealing with a knee injury that handed him a “limited” update for Wednesday practice. So his status is now pending for the week 11 showdown against the NFC South foe. Defensive back Kyler Gordon rose as the only one who did not practice. Wide receiver Luther Burden III, running back Kyle Monangai and DB Malik Muhammad emerged as full participants. But he sounds like he's taking his frustrations out after the Titans trade. Even he told The Rich Eisen Show he became shocked by the Titans move. Bears news: Jeffery Simmons lands on injury report before Week 11 Saints clash NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes The Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is suddenly banged up against the Saints, but was he a practice participant? Add ClutchPoints on Google Talia Sprague-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears ignited their defense in adding All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Head coach Ben Johnson has raved about the presence of the former Tennessee Titans star . But he landed on the NFL injury report before facing the New Orleans Saints. Still, Simmons has flexed his impact already on the Bears defensive line. Simmons lured his relentless pass rushing over from Nashville. “I'm on Year 8 here, I was the glue of trying to hold this locker room together,” he said. “I tried to give the organization so much on the field, in the locker room, at practice and in the community, and that's why I didn't think it would happen to me. I was pissed off.” Yet now he joins a franchise that's won four straight games and shares a 7-2 mark with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions. Chicago sits at third, though, in the current standings of the NFC North. Meanwhile, the Saints are one game behind in their NFC South race but sit at 3-6 overall. home.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
home.blurb: And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). home.headline: Bears’ Jeffery Simmons lands on injury report before Week 11 Saints clash
home.blurb: Simmons is dealing with a knee injury that handed him a “limited” update for Wednesday practice. So his status is now pending for the week 11 showdown against the NFC South foe. Defensive back Kyler Gordon rose as the only one who did not practice. Wide receiver Luther Burden III, running back Kyle Monangai and DB Malik Muhammad emerged as full participants. But he sounds like he's taking his frustrations out after the Titans trade. Even he told The Rich Eisen Show he became shocked by the Titans move. Bears news: Jeffery Simmons lands on injury report before Week 11 Saints clash NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes The Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is suddenly banged up against the Saints, but was he a practice participant? Add ClutchPoints on Google Talia Sprague-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears ignited their defense in adding All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Head coach Ben Johnson has raved about the presence of the former Tennessee Titans star . But he landed on the NFL injury report before facing the New Orleans Saints. Still, Simmons has flexed his impact already on the Bears defensive line. Simmons lured his relentless pass rushing over from Nashville. “I'm on Year 8 here, I was the glue of trying to hold this locker room together,” he said. “I tried to give the organization so much on the field, in the locker room, at practice and in the community, and that's why I didn't think it would happen to me. I was pissed off.” Yet now he joins a franchise that's won four straight games and shares a 7-2 mark with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions. Chicago sits at third, though, in the current standings of the NFC North. Meanwhile, the Saints are one game behind in their NFC South race but sit at 3-6 overall. home.headline: Bears get great news on Luther Burden III, Kyle Monangai ahead of Week 11
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears are coming out of their Week 10 bye with a 7-2 record, looking to keep pace with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions atop the division. It's not going to be easy, especially now that the Vikings have Kirk Cousins. But, fortunately for the Bears, they got some great news coming out of their Week 10 bye. Both might still be questionable, but Burden and Monangai look to be on track to suit up coming out of the bye. If that's the case, this offense might finally be fully healthy. Bears get great news on Luther Burden III and Kyle Monangai On the Bears injury report for Wednesday, which was an estimate as the team didn't actually hold practice, both Burden and Monangai were listed as full participants. Burden was recently cleared from concussion protocol after entering the protocol after Week 9 due to a hit late in the game. He's good to go for Week 11 with this news. Monangai is the much more interesting case, as the Bears have been without their No. 2 running back for much of the 2026 season. But now, with Monangai back and practicing in full, it appears he's good to go for Week 11. I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. As Saleh himself said after the team's latest loss, you aren't going to win allowing 40 points a game. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. Two of those losses were by seven points or fewer. The Cowboys' margin narrows with two starters missing. Right guard Tyler Booker and cornerback DaRon Bland are out. Tennessee ran no-huddle on 49% of its plays against Jacksonville, according to the Dallas Morning News. That tempo meets a Dallas run defense that allows 5.22 yards per carry, the league's worst mark, according to the Morning News. Tony Pollard, who spent five seasons with the Cowboys, has 628 rushing yards and six touchdowns this season, including 129 yards and three scores against Cleveland. Dallas can answer through the air. Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns against San Francisco, and George Pickens caught 11 passes for 145 yards and three scores. An early Cowboys lead would push Tennessee to chase points, and Ward has completed 38.9% of his passes under pressure, according to Pro Football Focus. If the game stays level, Dallas's tackling decides how long drives last. Wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) and safety Tony Adams (concussion) are questionable, and Saleh said Monday that the team was still evaluating both. Elic Ayomanor had five catches for 79 yards against Jacksonville, so Ward has other targets if Tate or Robinson sits. The defense is already thinner after the trades of Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker, according to the Associated Press. Bland's replacement: Durant or Speed at cornerback would test a Cowboys secondary that Schottenheimer said was beaten in man coverage. Dallas's defensive plan: Schottenheimer said simplifying the defense is a potential solution, so coverage calls and tackling are the details to watch. Tennessee is hoping all three can return for the game against the Dallas Cowboys. Carnell Tate Could Return Against Dallas For Tate, the next step is turning that optimism into clearance to play. Saleh's wording suggests a return is possible, but it was not a declaration that the receiver will suit up. Tennessee's practice reports and game designations will offer a clearer picture. Getting Tate back would give quarterback Cam Ward another receiving option at a time when the Titans are asking him to take control of the offense. Saleh explained Monday that Tennessee has given Ward more responsibility at the line of scrimmage. Having another receiver available would give the coaching staff more options as it continues that evaluation. That does not mean Tate's potential return fixes everything for Tennessee. The Titans still need to execute, and availability alone does not guarantee production. Still, having him in the lineup would be preferable to preparing for another game without him. For fans looking for an answer, Monday's comments stop short of providing one. They do, however, establish that the Cowboys game is a possibility for each player. away.blurb: Jacksonville's trade deadline splashes sitting out against Tennessee Those two additions round out a defensive unit that, when healthy, leaves Jacksonville with no real holes on paper as it chases a championship. A detail that's easy to lose track of at the trade deadline is how bye weeks shake out for traded players. Because teams take their byes at different points on the calendar, a player can get robbed of his bye entirely if his old team hadn't had one yet and his new team already did. On the flip side, some players luck into two. In the case of both Bates and Davis, neither had a bye this season until the Jaguars decided to hold them out against Tennessee. That gives them time to get up to speed mentally and to get some rest and recovery at the midpoint of the season before a push down the stretch, when it matters most for Jacksonville. Robert Saleh should be bringing it up in team meetings on Friday, again on Saturday, and in any meeting he has before kickoff on Sunday. The message writes itself: these guys don't respect you enough to deploy the starters they just went out and paid big for. They don't think they need them. That's how little they think of you. That gap gets wider when you look at the star power Tennessee will be missing. Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate has already been ruled out yet again with his shoulder injury. The reporting when he sat out the Cincinnati Bengals game in Week 8 was that the Titans wanted him to roll that absence into the bye week and get roughly three full weeks of rest. He clearly isn't quite ready to come back. Linebackers Anthony Hill and Cody Barton are both ruled out as well. That means Cedric Gray gets a big prove-it week, with Tennessee running thin at the position. The offensive line takes a hit, too. Star left guard Peter Skoronski is out, and neither Fernando Carmona nor swing backup Jackson Slater has returned from the injuries that knocked them out at right guard. So the Titans will be without either of their starting guards. Atonio Mafi, who has held down right guard admirably, likely stays on the right side, and yet another depth player (technically guard No. 5 on the depth chart) will step in on the left, whoever Tennessee deems worthy of the role. What is a “Push” in Sports Betting Super Bowl Prop Bets Double Result Bets More NCAAB March Madness Odds Predictions & Picks Schedule & Results Stats Scoring Everything About March Madness 2026 Tennis How to Bet on March Madness Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Detroit Lions Tampa Bay Buccaneers 3-6 Detroit Lions 7-2 Match Overview Match Game Preview Luke Lindholm Last Updated: 4 hours ago The Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) enter Week 11 off their bye, but their road matchup against the Detroit Lions (7-2) won't be easy. Detroit is riding a five-game winning streak and just dominated the New England Patriots 35-10 in Munich last Sunday. RB Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and scored two touchdowns, while also adding 99 receiving yards. WR Amon-Ra St. Brown also caught two TDs. However, DE Aidan Hutchinson tore his right ACL while celebrating a first-quarter sack, and he's out for the season. Luckily for Detroit, Tampa Bay is also dealing with a major injury. QB Baker Mayfield is dealing with a foot injury suffered in the Bucs' Week 9 loss to the Chicago Bears. He was in and out of a walking boot during the bye week, and reports state that it is looking likely for undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels to start. Daniels was 1-2 earlier this season as a starter while Baker missed time with a thumb injury, so he at least won't be going into this game completely blind. Buccaneers vs. Lions Kickoff, Weather, TV, Streaming Info Kickoff is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Ford Field in Detroit. FOX carries the American broadcast, while Canadians can stream nationwide through DAZN's NFL Game Pass. Weather will not be a factor because Ford Field is a domed stadium. NFL Betting Odds, Point Spread, Trends Detroit is a seven-point favourite, with the Lions at -110 and the Buccaneers +7 at an identical -110 price. Tampa Bay Buccaneers @ Detroit Lions On the money line, the Lions are -355 favourites , while the Bucs are +280 underdogs. The total is 43.5, with the Over at -115 and the Under at -105 . These numbers were much different earlier in the week, as Mayfield was still in line to play. Tampa Bay is 4-5 against the spread this season, while Detroit is 4-4-1. The Over has chased in five out of both teams' nine contests this season. If this game is close entering the fourth quarter, expect the Lions to pull away. The Bucs are 0-4 this season when within seven points entering the final quarter. NFL Player Odds and Props Gibbs became the first player to tally 1,000 rushing yards this season last week, and he is now tied for the most rushing TDs in the league with 11. The Bucs allow the fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL (79.1), so it will be interesting to see if the Lions star RB can get going on Sunday. Gibbs' rushing yards line is 90.5 ( -110 both ways ). I'd avoid betting his rushing yards line and look towards his receiving yards total at 27.5 ( -110 both ways). RB Bucky Irving has tallied 825 rushing yards and seven touchdowns this season, and he has carried the ball 71 times over Tampa's last three games. He has cashed the Over on his carries total in 12 of his last 15 games. Irving's total carries sit at 16.5 ( -110 both ways) , and I absolutely love the Over, as they should rely on him early and often with a rookie QB. The Bucs have the most rushing yards per game (163.9), and they set a franchise record with 324 rushing yards earlier this season when they beat the Falcons 16-0; they didn't attempt a single pass in that game. Understandably, they rank dead last in the NFL in passing yards per game (141.9). This Buccaneers offence isn't elite by any means, but their defence is one of the league's best units. Tampa Bay allows 19.8 PPG (sixth in the NFL), and they lead the league in takeaways (21). The Lions offence should be feared. They're scoring 28.6 PPG (sixth in the NFL), and they have the third-most yards per game in the league (392.4). Although the offence often gets most of the glamour, the defence has quietly held four straight opponents to 21 points or fewer, and Detroit is 6-0 when it forces a turnover. These stats matter when they're facing a rookie QB. Detroit's biggest issue is their injury report. Getting Brian Branch back last week from his Achilles tear was a big boost to the secondary, but All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell is on IR (neck), Hutchinson is out for the season, and Kerby Joseph (knee), D.J. Reed (hip), and Cade Mays (ankle) did not travel to Germany last week. Bucs vs. Lions Week 11 Score Prediction Drake Maye exiting the Germany game early didn't help my Over last week, and if I learned anything with that loss it was to not count on an offence without their starting QB. Tampa's defence can keep this game close, but expect a low-scoring affair. I'll bet the Under and tune into a few of Sunday's other games featuring more offensive star power. away.blurb: It was reported over the weekend that quarterback Baker Mayfield was "in and out" of a walking boot over the team's bye week, and his status for Week 11 at the Detroit Lions was uncertain. Rapoport appeared on ESPN's NFL Live to deliver the news, making a point to say he isn't ruling Mayfield out this week, only that things are trending in that direction. Mayfield's status will be closely monitored all week. Wednesday's injury report should be very telling. If Mayfield can practice in any capacity, it may be a good sign for his chances to play on Sunday. If not, he would still have two more opportunities to practice before official injury designations come out on Friday. According to Ian Rapoport, Mayfield is trending towards not playing on Sunday, and the Bucs are preparing for undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels to take over once again. Daniels, who won the QB2 job after a stellar preseason, was forced into action earlier this season when Mayfield missed three games with a dislocated thumb. The rookie went 1-2 in his stint as starter, mostly playing like a poised veteran and not an undrafted rookie. "There have been some thoughts about maybe him playing. It's still up in the air, but based on what I know, it seems to be trending toward Jalon Daniels stepping in for Baker this week." In his first three seasons with the Bucs, Mayfield missed a grand total of zero games. This year has been a different story, with Tampa's franchise QB already missing three games and appearing likely to miss another. It has been a trying and disappointing season for the Bucs , and Mayfield's injuries and underwhelming play have been big reasons why. Mayfield sustained the new injuries during Tampa's Week 9 loss to the Chicago Bears . Although he didn't leave the game, there were instances in the fourth quarter where Mayfield was slow to get up after being hit and sacked and was in obvious pain. Mayfield's newest injury is being labeled a foot strain and it looks like the bye week won't afford him enough time to get back on the field against the Lions. However, as Rapoport notes, Mayfield is a tough guy who consistently plays through injuries and still has a chance to suit up on Sunday. Mayfield suffered the injury during last week's 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears on Sunday Night Football. It's unclear exactly when Mayfield got hurt; he never left the game and ran in a two-point conversion to tie it with just under three minutes remaining. The 31-year-old finished the game with 18 of 32 completions for 243 yards and no touchdown passes against two interceptions. The Sunday night contest was his third game back in the lineup after he missed three contests due to a thumb injury. Mayfield ranks 29th in passer rating and last in EPA/dropback among 31 qualifying quarterbacks this season, according to TruMedia. away.headline: The Chiefs face a rare in-season opportunity with the Cardinals coming to KC
away.blurb: The Cardinals are without their leading wide receiver, Michael Wilson, who injured his back earlier this month and is out for the season. And first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, the running back, is on injured reserve because of an ankle issue. The Chiefs are 16- to 16.5-point favorites against the Cardinals on Sunday. Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. The Chiefs may rest injured players before playing the Bills on Thanksgiving. You don’t have to be a soothsayer to know that Chiefs coach Andy Reid will be looking forward to the challenge of playing the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. It’s what Reid says each week about the Chiefs’ next opponent. The oddsmakers aren’t so sure it’ll be a challenge for the Chiefs. BetMGM has the Chiefs as a 16-point favorite , while DraftKings has the line at 16 1/2 points . It’s rare to see a team be favored by more than two scores, but that’s where things stand. And it makes for an interesting and rare NFL opportunity facing the Chiefs: Should they rest players Sunday because of a short turnaround into their next game? After playing the Cardinals, the Chiefs will take on the AFC-leading Bills in Buffalo on Thanksgiving. The Chiefs will never publicly say they are pondering resting players given the strength of their opponent, but the Cardinals, 3-7, are down on their luck. After picking up road wins against the Chargers, Rams and Cowboys through the first eight weeks of the season, Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. Ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Cardinals dealt their top quarterback (Jacoby Brissett) and wide receiver (Marvin Harrison Jr.). There were 15 players listed on the Cardinals’ injury report last week ahead of Arizona’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. That includes safety Andrew Wingard, who is not expected to play against the Chiefs, according to the team’s website. Four offensive linemen were on that injured list, including Hjalte Froholdt and Jon Gaines II. In the Cardinals’ 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday, linebacker Jordan Burch suffered a season-ending knee injury. Rookie Carson Beck will start at quarterback for the Cardinals because backup Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending injury. Beck has attempted 18 career NFL passes, and his backups are 40-year-old Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. The Cardinals will enter Sunday’s game with the 29th-ranked scoring offense and 31st-ranked scoring defense. The Chiefs also have injuries, and a number of players were hurt during Sunday’s game against the Falcons: guard Trey Smith (concussion), tight end Jared Wiley (broken ankle) and Travis Kelce (calf). Also, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane landed hard on his back. And the Chiefs played without running back Kenneth Walker, who has a groin injury. Regardless of what the oddsmakers say, no game is a gimme, but the Chiefs might have enough firepower against a short-handed Cardinals team that they could let Walker rest.

away.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. home.headline: The Chiefs face a rare in-season opportunity with the Cardinals coming to KC
home.blurb: The Cardinals are without their leading wide receiver, Michael Wilson, who injured his back earlier this month and is out for the season. And first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, the running back, is on injured reserve because of an ankle issue. The Chiefs are 16- to 16.5-point favorites against the Cardinals on Sunday. Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. The Chiefs may rest injured players before playing the Bills on Thanksgiving. You don’t have to be a soothsayer to know that Chiefs coach Andy Reid will be looking forward to the challenge of playing the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. It’s what Reid says each week about the Chiefs’ next opponent. The oddsmakers aren’t so sure it’ll be a challenge for the Chiefs. BetMGM has the Chiefs as a 16-point favorite , while DraftKings has the line at 16 1/2 points . It’s rare to see a team be favored by more than two scores, but that’s where things stand. And it makes for an interesting and rare NFL opportunity facing the Chiefs: Should they rest players Sunday because of a short turnaround into their next game? After playing the Cardinals, the Chiefs will take on the AFC-leading Bills in Buffalo on Thanksgiving. The Chiefs will never publicly say they are pondering resting players given the strength of their opponent, but the Cardinals, 3-7, are down on their luck. After picking up road wins against the Chargers, Rams and Cowboys through the first eight weeks of the season, Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. Ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Cardinals dealt their top quarterback (Jacoby Brissett) and wide receiver (Marvin Harrison Jr.). There were 15 players listed on the Cardinals’ injury report last week ahead of Arizona’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. That includes safety Andrew Wingard, who is not expected to play against the Chiefs, according to the team’s website. Four offensive linemen were on that injured list, including Hjalte Froholdt and Jon Gaines II. In the Cardinals’ 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday, linebacker Jordan Burch suffered a season-ending knee injury. Rookie Carson Beck will start at quarterback for the Cardinals because backup Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending injury. Beck has attempted 18 career NFL passes, and his backups are 40-year-old Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. The Cardinals will enter Sunday’s game with the 29th-ranked scoring offense and 31st-ranked scoring defense. The Chiefs also have injuries, and a number of players were hurt during Sunday’s game against the Falcons: guard Trey Smith (concussion), tight end Jared Wiley (broken ankle) and Travis Kelce (calf). Also, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane landed hard on his back. And the Chiefs played without running back Kenneth Walker, who has a groin injury. Regardless of what the oddsmakers say, no game is a gimme, but the Chiefs might have enough firepower against a short-handed Cardinals team that they could let Walker rest.

home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid's injury update after Week 10's win over Falcons spells bad news for 2024 NFL Draft pick
home.blurb: Wiley was carted to the locker room during the first quarter of the blowout win over the Falcons. The team dealt with a few more injuries as the game went on. Reid confirmed that Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye, which was clear on TV. He finished the game and will ultimately be ok. As for CB Mansoor Delane, it seems like he was pulled more so out of an abundance of caution. "He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area," Reid said. "I think he was scared more than anything. He's going to be alright, though." Another injury setback for Delane's shoulder would be troubling, but he sounds like he avoided anything serious. As for Wiley, this is the type of injury that could prematurely end his Chiefs career. As a rookie out of TCU in 2024, Wiley suffered a season-ending ACL injury during practice. That injury really took away the remainder of his rookie season and limited him during the 2025 NFL season as well. It wasn't until this offseason that he felt like he was getting back to himself. However, that never really came to fruition in on-field production. Now, with the ankle fracture that will almost certainly end his season, Wiley is heading for another long rehab and recovery. A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of TCU, Wiley is listed at 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds. The Chiefs have appeared in 50 combined regular-season and postseason games since the start of the 2024 NFL season. Whether it has been injury or a healthy scratch, Wiley has played in 15 of 50 possible games during that timeframe. Wiley is likely slated for IR with the fractured ankle, with eight more games left in the 2026 NFL regular season. As for how the team will adapt to Wiley's loss, it likely opens a needed roster spot, with Omarr Norman-Lott slated to return soon . Kansas City has three tight ends on the 53-man roster currently, with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, and Jake Briningstool. They have one tight end on the practice squad in the International Player Pathway Program, Thomas Odukoya.
