home.blurb: Ex-Chiefs' Tyreek Hill Shares Medical Update Ahead of Desired NFL Return Unlock the latest Heavy on Chiefs news — direct to your inbox. The Kansas City Chiefs remain a potential destination for idiosyncratic wide receiver Tyreek Hill, who is still in the process of recovering from a torn ACL suffered back in Sep. 2025. With his agent Drew Rosenhaus having been in negotiations with teams to have him sign in the imminent future back in early October , it appears that there may have been some minor relapse in his recovery, or at least teams are wary of adding the controversial wideout prior to him being completely medically cleared. Tyreek Hill Goes to Germany to See ‘Healing Hans' In the pursuit of being so at some point this season, Hill has flown to Germany to meet with a doctor known in the trade as ‘ Healing Hans ‘, who has also worked with other top athletes such as Usain Bolt and the NFL's own Christian McCaffrey. The comeback continues. 🙏🏿 Dr. Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, to go by his full name, often uses semi-unorthodox and untraditional medical methods to help athletes, which span recommendations from Bolt, German soccer legend Franz Beckenbauer and world championship gold-medalist sprinter Tyson Gay. ‘Healing Hans' at 84 years old has seemingly seen it all and dealt with athletes that have suffered a wide, wide range of conditions. Will This Help Speed Up Tyreek Hill's Recovery? The exact nature of the medical treatment Hill was not revealed, although some practices were shown in the video , including that of something appearing to be injected into the former Chiefs man's left leg. The full timetable for his recovery has not been announced, although Rosenhaus admitted last week that Hill still has a " few more weeks " until he is medically cleared to play. Hill will be hoping that his rendezvous helps speed up and solidify that recovery so that he can aim to play some part in the 2026 season, ideally for a playoff-bound franchise. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) head to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. Smith’s availability is especially significant because the Eagles badly need another proven weapon alongside Saquon Barkley to make life easier for Milton against a Pittsburgh defense featuring T.J. Watt and one of the NFL’s better pass rushes. Beyond Pittsburgh’s attempt to rebound and Philadelphia’s effort to stop its seven-game skid, the matchup carries a fascinating piece of Pennsylvania rivalry history. The Eagles lead the all-time series 50-29-3, and Pittsburgh has endured an extraordinary drought in Philadelphia. The Steelers have not won in Philly since 1965. They have lost their last 11 games against the Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love. Philadelphia has also dominated the two most recent meetings, winning 27-13 in Philadelphia on Dec. 15, 2024, after a 35-13 home victory in 2022; Pittsburgh’s last win in the series was a 38-29 victory at Heinz Field in 2020. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. picks.headline: 2026 Steelers Preview: Week 11 vs. the Philadelphia Eagles
picks.blurb: Login/Register Home The 2026 NFL regular season is in full swing, and it's time to preview the Pittsburgh Steelers schedule ahead of every game this season. I'm going to revisit my offseason breakdown of every game on the Steelers schedule as a preview for the upcoming game. I'll be updating the odds and quarterbacks expected to play in the contest, and will only list my offseason prediction. My in-season prediction always comes both on the Steelers Preview podcast Thursday night, as well as on my Friday “Let's Ride” podcast. Here is the detailed breakdown of the Steelers 2026 regular season, continuing with an AFC vs. NFC game vs. the Eagles in Philadelphia. Week 11 at the Philadelphia Eagles Date: Sunday, November 22nd – 1:00pm EST Betting Line: Early Line: Eagles (-5.5) / Total: 42.5 Current Line: Steelers (-4.5) / Total: 38.5 Last Meeting: 12/15/24 – Eagles 27, Steelers 13 Overall Series Record: Philadelphia Eagles lead series 50-29-3 2026 Records: Steelers: 6-3 Projected Starting QB Matchup: Aaron Rodgers vs. Joe Milton or Tanner McKee Analysis: I wanted to convince myself that the Steelers would be able to go into Philadelphia and slay their proverbial dragon. After all, they haven't won in Philadelphia since the Lyndon B. Johnson administration. However, even my optimistic brain can't see a path for them to win the game on the other side of the state. Barring injury, the Eagles defense is going to be a top-notch team in 2026, and while the loss of AJ Brown hurts the offense, they will still have plenty of play makers at their disposal, mainly with a healthy Saquon Barkley. To put it in simple terms, the Eagles are a team the Steelers just don't match up well against. Could they shock the world and break the horrible streak of losing in Philadelphia? I guess anything is possible, but I can't say I am predicting that to take place. I've always said if you could hand pick a loss on the schedule, losing to an NFC opponent on the road would be the choice you should make. And that's exactly what I am predicting in this Week 11 game. Does this loss derail the entire season? I don't think so, but it certainly is a bump in the road. The Steelers will have to dust themselves off quickly as they return to Pittsburgh for a Black Friday game at home vs. the Denver Broncos coming up in Week 12. Prediction: Eagles 26, Steelers 20 Clearly things change from the offseason and schedule release to the upcoming game, but no one saw the collapse of the Eagles in the preseason. How could anyone predict Jalen Hurts being put on Injured Reserve (IR) for blood clots and All-Pro offensive tackle Lane Johnson retiring. I may have thought the Eagles would take a step back, but 2-7 at their bye week was not in my mind. While most would assume the Steelers should dominate the lesser than Eagles, especially after their trade activity, I'm not about to think this game will be easy. I find it difficult to even believe the decades long slump in Philadelphia will end. The Steelers are coming off a drubbing, and the Eagles are coming off their bye week. away.headline: Steelers place Mason McCormick on injured reserve
away.blurb: With McCormick now on IR, the Steelers have an opening on their 53-man roster. After Pittsburgh opened the 21-day practice window for wide receivers Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson, as well as rookie guard Gennings Dunker, earlier in the day, the team could leave the vacant spot available for one of those three players’ eventual activation. Steelers utility lineman Spencer Anderson is expected to start at left guard for the team while McCormick misses time. The earliest McCormick can return to the lineup would be the Steelers’ Dec. 20 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, although a report from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport on Wednesday indicated the Steelers hope McCormick can return for the playoffs, which don’t begin until mid-January. The Steelers got good news regarding offensive lineman Mason McCormick early Wednesday, with the starting left guard suffering a dislocated ankle instead of a fracture — avoiding surgery after a gruesome-looking injury on Sunday versus the Bengals. However, McCormick will still be missing the Steelers’ next four games at minimum, with the team placing him on injured reserve Wednesday, Pittsburgh announced .

away.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers cut ties with former Giants wide receiver
away.blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers have cut ties with wide receiver Isaiah Hodgins , who was on the practice squad with the team since Week 2. Hodgins was added when Max Hurleman went down with a hamstring injury, but with Hurleman’s return, the team has decided to move on. A sixth-round pick out of Oregon State by the Buffalo Bills, Hodgins has experience playing outside and in the slot with the teams. He has 70 receptions for 749 receiving yards and eight touchdowns in his career. Hurleman along with Brandon Johnson still remain on the Steelers’ practice squad. The Steelers have seen Hurleman earn some praise over the last week with Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy giving him notable praise. Hodgins never was elevated from the practice squad, unlike Johnson and Brandon Smith. Smith remains on the 53-man roster. Hodgins was with the Steelers last year but the Giants signed him off the practice squad. The Giants moved on from Hodgins earlier this year before he landed with the Steelers. Hodgins spent his first three seasons in the NFL with the Bills, but was cut in the middle of 2022 when the Giants claimed him off waivers. He would spent the next three years there until the expiration of his rookie contract. Standing at 6-foot-4, Hodgins has unique size for the position. His father, James, was a fullback and that gives him a level of experience around the game since the time he was a kid. away.headline: Steelers could get WR reinforcements vs. Eagles with latest injury news
away.blurb: MORE: How Long Will Mason McCormick Be Out With Ankle Injury? Metcalf has caught under half (35 of 71) of his targets from Rodgers in 2026 so far, on pace for a career-worst season. Rookie Germie Bernard had a breakout game against the Buccaneers, but has otherwise made a limited impact. Depth options like Smith and Ben Skowronek have been just that, not emerging as go-to weapons for Rodgers. Pittman has appeared in just three games so far; he was placed on IR on Oct. 10, dealing with plantar fasciitis in his left foot before Mike McCarthy said he "aggravated a foot injury." After landing with the Steelers via trade from the Colts, then inking an extension, Pittman hasn't yet panned out as a starting receiver in Pittsburgh. Wilson, meanwhile, flashed some growing chemistry with Rodgers against the Bengals in September (three catches, 60 yards, TD) and against the Browns in October (three catches, 74 yards, TD). But he was also placed on IR on Oct. 17 due to a finger injury, out since then. The good news for Pittsburgh: both Wilson and Pittman are on the mend, as McCarthy said Wednesday that the window for each receiver to return from IR has been opened, per Brooke Pryor. The Steelers head coach said that "it’ll take evaluating them all week" to determine the status of Wilson, Pittman Max Hurleman and Gennings Dunker for Week 11 against the Eagles, per Pryor, so it's no guarantee that any of those players are making a full return quite yet. However, once Wilson and Pittman can return soon, they will be welcome reinforcements for an offense that needs some explosiveness. One of the clear weaknesses for the Steelers ' offense this season has been production from the wide receiver room. While Jaylen Warren has had a breakout season in the backfield, and the Pat Freiermuth-Darnell Washington tight end duo has been among the NFL's best, Aaron Rodgers hasn't found much success targeting his wideouts. It was a trend that continued in a blowout Week 10 loss, with D.K. Metcalf and Brandon Smith leading all wide receivers with just two catches each. As the Steelers prepare for a road matchup in Philadelphia this Sunday, though, they could be getting some much-needed reinforcements based on the latest injury developments. Here's what to know about potential returns for multiple Steelers receivers. Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson Injury Updates The Steelers opted not to make a move for a wideout at the trade deadline despite reportedly considering an addition at the position. With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson missing extended periods with injuries, that's left them thin at wide receiver, especially with Metcalf's struggles. With the wide receivers practicing again, the Steelers could have a deeper passing game again in the weeks to come. home.headline: Eagles rumors: The hot trade candidate who’s in line to make bank
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles are trying to navigate a season where injuries have hurt them, and it’s affected their overall play. At this point, it wouldn’t be a surprise if they were banking on preparing for next season, and it was obvious that the future was in play when they traded Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars at the deadline. The Eagles were also getting trade interest from Moro Ojomo, but they elected to keep him. Not only that, but there’s a chance that they strike a new deal with him in the offseason, according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. “Another interesting name is Eagles defensive lineman Moro Ojomo,” Fowler wrote. “Like Washington, he wasn’t a household name to enter the season. But Ojomo garnered significant trade interest this offseason and at the deadline, and Philly opted to keep him. It would like to pay him, too. Let’s see if the Eagles can get that done. Explosive 3-4 defensive ends get paid in free agency. Ojomo can use a former Eagle Milton Williams — who signed a four-year, $104 million free agency deal with New England in 2025 — as a roadmap of sorts.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The trenches have always been an area where the Eagles have thrived, so it wouldn’t be a surprise if they brought back Ojomo next season. Other than that, the Eagles may be looking to upgrade several positions when the season is over. There’s no question that they’ll need some more offensive firepower, and if they end up with a good draft pick, selecting a skill player should be at the top of the list. Howie Roseman has already raised eyebrows after he linked up with Darian Mensah before his game, and that could lead people to assume the Eagles are in the business of drafting a quarterback. home.blurb: Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. Smith’s availability is especially significant because the Eagles badly need another proven weapon alongside Saquon Barkley to make life easier for Milton against a Pittsburgh defense featuring T.J. The team that beat the Detroit Lions and Philadelphia Eagles in consecutive games felt like a different team from the one we'd seen in the last few weeks. But the Panthers got back into the win column with a clutch 20-17 victory on the road against the New Orleans Saints. That exorcised some Superdome demons and kept the Panthers in first place in the NFC South for the time being. The Panthers would love to keep stacking wins. They want to win the division first and foremost, but they also want to prove they're a good team regardless, and ending with the franchise's first winning record since 2017 would be excellent. Can they get back to .500 against the Baltimore Ravens this week? Week 11 NFL odds have Panthers favored at home vs. Ravens Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) drops back to pass against the New Orleans Saints | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It's not often that the Carolina Panthers are favored, and when they are, they usually stumble (see: Tampa Bay Buccaneers loss earlier this year). Nevertheless, it is good to be favored in a given game, especially a home tilt. The Baltimore Ravens are not the usual Ravens. Lamar Jackson is out, and they've stumbled to a subpar record after facing the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football. That fact, as well as the slightly short week and road trip, may be why the Panthers are favored. Carolina is -130 to win outright ( DraftKings ). Baltimore is +110 on the moneyline. The spread is 2.5 points, and the Panthers are -110 to cover. The Ravens are -110 to cover as well, so the margins are thin. The total has been set at 44.5. The over is -108, and the under is -112. That means that oddsmakers expect the Panthers to win a close one by a score of 23-20, give or take. It should be tight between these two teams. The Panthers have fared well against backup quarterbacks this year. They dominated both Cooper Rush and Tanner McKee, and that was before the defensive coordinator change that seems to have sparked a defensive turnaround. away.headline: NFL fans react to Ravens’ rumored plan for Lamar Jackson’s return after thumb injury
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens believe Lamar Jackson has a chance to return from his broken right thumb for their Week 16 game against the Cleveland Browns on Dec. 27 if his rehab goes smoothly, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week. Lamar Jackson’s Road From Buffalo Toward a Possible Browns Return In a statement the team released that day, head coach Jesse Minter called recovery timelines “challenging to predict” and said, “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Minter added, “We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season.” Graziano’s report hinges on Jackson’s progress in the same way, leaving the Browns game at M&T Bank Stadium a possibility rather than a set date for his return. For another fan, the calendar is the problem, since a return against the Browns would leave Jackson only two more regular-season games after that one. A Dec. 27 return would be near the optimistic end of Jackson’s reported recovery timetable, though the Ravens have emphasized that his progress, rather than a fixed date, will determine when he can play again. The report comes with Baltimore at 4-6, days after a 23-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who had not won a game before Monday night. Despite the prospect of Jackson returning for the final stretch of the regular season, several fans who responded to the report argued that the Ravens should keep him sidelined and focus on having him healthy for 2027. Jackson’s injury came on Baltimore’s first offensive play of the Nov. 1 game at Buffalo, a 36-10 loss, when his throwing hand caught the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau as he threw. On Nov. 13, the Ravens said the thumb was dislocated and broken and that the injury typically carries a recovery of six to 10 weeks. Sources told ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Jackson had undergone surgery the week before. Fans Point to the Baltimore Ravens’ Slide and Jackson’s Long-Term Health “Week 16 is so late. Just shut him down and run it back next year,” the fan wrote. Baltimore’s form has added to the argument. The Ravens sit fourth in the AFC North and have lost five straight games, including the Buffalo game in which Jackson was hurt and both games since. Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore acquired in a trade, started in Jackson’s place in the loss to the Chargers. “It’s already over … just take the rest of the season off,” another fan responded. Jackson’s health is another piece of it. A high ankle sprain had already cost him three games before the thumb injury, and he has played just 14 full quarters this season. A fan pointed to that history: “Yea bro let’s have Lamar play meaningless games in a lost season after 2 major injuries.” Others looked straight ahead to next season. “What’s the point to play him at that point, come back ’27 stronger,” one fan wrote. home.headline: Carolina Panthers star Jaelan Phillips punctuates big comeback with NFC honor
home.blurb: Phillips was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 10, according to a release from the NFL. The team’s most sought-after free-agent pickup in March set season-highs in tackles (five) and tackles for loss (three), while adding a sack and a fumble recovery in the 20-17, potentially season-changing win . He nearly added another sack — he was called for a questionable horse-collar penalty in the fourth quarter that nullified his takedown of Saints quarterback Tyler Shough — and was hoping to turn that fumble recovery into a return for a TD. (”I tried,” he said with a smile when asked about his touchdown aspirations.) Maybe it was because he felt like himself again, ripping around offensive tackles and bulldozing backfield-blockers. Maybe it was because he was on the field at all — he’d missed the previous three weeks due to a hamstring injury. “That’s part of it,” he said in the postgame locker room Sunday, at first alluding to the injuries. “And then also just to have good disruption, defense is flying around.” He shrugged. “When you make plays, it’s fun to play.” Suffice to say Phillips made several plays Sunday. And on Wednesday, he was rewarded for it. Phillips’ stat-line marked only the third player in the league this season to record three TFLs, a sack and a fumble recovery in the same game. It also marked the first-career DPOW honor for Phillips and the second DPOW honor for the Panthers this year; linebacker Devin Lloyd , another free-agency acquisition, earned the honor in Week 2. The Panthers are the only team in the NFL this season with two linebackers who won this award. Wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan also earned the honor for the Panthers after Week 4. The news is a big validation point for Phillips, who when healthy has been a game-changer with the Panthers — but who has also battled injury a bunch this season. He suffered a hamstring injury Week 4 against the Detroit Lions, came back ready to play after the bye against the Eagles, and then aggravated the same injury. He missed the next three games thereafter — a stretch that saw three straight losses (including when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran rampant against the Panthers for 258 rushing yards) and also the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero . Since the departure of Evero and the appointment of interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash, the front-seven for the Panthers have been wreaking havoc in the backfield much more. The Panthers’ first glimpse of Phillips in Wash’s system was against the Saints, and it went swimmingly for the player who signed a four-year, $120 million contract . Prior to Week 7 — his first entire-game absence of 2026 — Phillips had 18 total pressures; in Week 10, he notched nearly half of that total (a season-high eight pressures, according to Pro Football Reference). The Panthers (3-4) still sit atop the NFC South, but in order to hold onto their station, they’ll likely need to emerge from Bank of America Stadium with a victory against one of the powers of the AFC — the Denver Broncos (6-2). The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. The Chargers (1-8) snapped an 11-game losing streak with a 23-20 win at Baltimore on Monday night, while the Jets (2-8) have lost five straight. Geno Smith left last Sunday's loss to the Bills twice, but imaging did not show a major ankle injury, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The strongest supported case for the Chargers starts at the line of scrimmage. Omarion Hampton ran 22 times for 105 yards at Baltimore, and Justin Herbert added 51 yards. The Jets allow 135 rushing yards a game, 30th in the league, and gave up 201 to Buffalo. That path has limits. The Chargers rank 32nd in scoring at 16.0 points a game and 31st in sacks allowed, and Herbert has thrown 11 interceptions. The Jets' pass defense ranks fifth at 197 yards allowed a game, so Los Angeles still needs a clean day through the air if the run game stalls. New York's route to an upset runs through touchdowns. The Jets scored 12 points in each of their last two games and went 0-for-3 in the red zone across them. Smith has 12 touchdown passes and three interceptions this season, which makes his availability the biggest variable in their offense. Jets vs Chargers win probabilities These percentages are the market's implied probabilities , so 61% means traders see the Chargers winning about six times in ten. Smith's status could shift both numbers before kickoff. How could Jets vs Chargers unfold? The opening drives could show which plan holds. The Chargers scored on their first possession Monday, a six-play, 63-yard drive that ended with Herbert's 22-yard touchdown run. Jim Harbaugh later kept the offense on the field on fourth down twice during a second-quarter drive that ended with Hampton's touchdown. The Jets trailed at halftime against both Kansas City and Buffalo, so an early Chargers lead would test them again. Coordinator Brian Duker called defensive plays for the first time last Sunday. Azareye'h Thomas intercepted Josh Allen, only the Jets' second interception of the season. Pressure is the Jets' other lever. They have six sacks in their last five games, according to NFL.com, while the Chargers have allowed 33 in nine games, including eight against Houston. Herbert took two sacks at Baltimore, so New York needs its rush to reach him sooner. Game state will steer the rest. If the Jets fall behind by two scores, Smith or rookie Cade Klubnik must throw against a Chargers defense that has intercepted eight passes, tied for seventh in the league. A close game keeps Hampton's carries central. The Chargers have six days between games after Monday night in Baltimore, a day fewer than the Jets. What is the latest team news? Both teams carry injury questions into Sunday, and the Jets' is at quarterback. What is the latest on the Jets? Smith missed a series for a concussion evaluation, returned, then left for good when his left ankle rolled in the third quarter, according to The Associated Press. Imaging did not show a major injury, and the hope is that he starts, ESPN reported. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Smith remains the starter if healthy. If Smith cannot play, Klubnik would make his first NFL start. The rookie completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with an interception and three sacks in his debut, ESPN reported. ESPN's injury listings show receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) and guard Dylan Parham (knee) as questionable, and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) and cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. (illness) as out. Glenn said Smith, Cooper and Parham all had imaging tests. What is the latest on the Chargers? Receiver Ladd McConkey was absent at Baltimore with a back injury, according to ESPN, and his availability for Sunday is unresolved. Tre' Harris filled the gap with five catches for 86 yards in the first half there. ESPN's listings show receiver Brenen Thompson, defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe, cornerback Isas Waxter and safety Kendall Williamson as out, and cornerback Rodney Shelley (ankle) as questionable. Three rookies started on the offensive line Monday, ESPN reported. What could decide Jets vs Chargers? Three matchups carry most of the weight, and the first one decides who controls the clock. They currently sit at 7-2, are in the hunt for the AFC West title and the top seed in the AFC. Even better is the week off should allow the Broncos to get players back from injury, especially on defense. All of this to say Denver is in a great spot. Now come the hated Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The Broncos want to build on this great start to the season and carry the momentum over from the bye this Sunday against their rivals. Denver is a massive -10-point home favorite against the Raiders (4-6) at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the under at -115. Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Just win, baby! (By starting fast offensively) The best way to put pressure on a rookie quarterback is to make the Las Vegas offense one-dimensional. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense can do their part by starting Sunday's game fast offensively and finishing drives with touchdowns. We saw glimpses of this against the Carolina Panthers, with some deep shots early by Nix, but Denver had to kick a field goal on the opening drive. Replicate that this Sunday, but finish the opening drive with a touchdown. And then do it again. And then again. Add to the pressure that the Broncos defense will undoubtedly bring on the rookie QB. — Ian St. Clair Get after Fernando Mendoza Last week, Fernando Mendoza got his first career NFL start against a fierce Seattle Seahawks defense. Prior to Mendoza being a starter, the Raiders' offensive line only allowed 11 sacks when Kirk Cousins was quarterback. Last Sunday, with the 2026 NFL Draft's top pick under center, they gave up six to the Seahawks. If Denver wants to win the game, their defensive front seven has to dominate. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph needs to throw everything he can at the rookie signal caller and rattle him early and often. — Christopher Hart Keep feeding Jonah Coleman I don't need to discuss numbers. Just look at how much better the offense is when Coleman gets his touches. Whether he's running the ball or catching passes, he gives the offense a weapon that forces the defense to respect what Denver is doing in the trenches, thus opening up the opportunities for Bo Nix to push the ball downfield. — Adam Malnati Blow a team out for once I know, I know. Now, it's Raiders week, and my key to the game is simple. Score more points than the Raiders. Denver is 7-0 when it does that and 0-2 when it does not. Using advanced analytics, I say the Broncos have a 100% chance to win on Sunday if they score more points than the Raiders. away.headline: Fernando Mendoza's 6 sacks shape Las Vegas Raiders' Denver prep
away.blurb: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) left the game after two catches for 18 yards and did not return after halftime. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak called the injury significant but said Bowers was day to day, putting added weight on the rest of the passing game as Mendoza prepares for his first road start. Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza took six sacks in his first NFL start, making blitz recognition and protection communication central to his preparation for the Denver Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 22. Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards and added a rushing touchdown in the 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Locked On Raiders host Qiant Myers viewed the debut as encouraging evidence that Mendoza can grow into the long-term answer at quarterback. Myers also focused on the rookie’s difficulty identifying slot pressure, arguing Mendoza must either recognize a free blitzer sooner or ensure the protection accounts for it. The pressure did not erase the positives from Mendoza’s first start. He gave the Raiders an early lead with a 10-yard touchdown run, and the team led 10-7 at halftime. But the offense managed 24 yards over its next seven possessions, a second-half slide that left little margin for a rookie quarterback facing repeated pressure. Myers argued that Mendoza’s presence changes the franchise’s offseason priorities. Rather than entering another quarterback search, he said, the Raiders can use the remaining schedule to evaluate how well they can protect Mendoza, add reliable receiving options, and build a more consistent defense around him. – Kubiak said Bowers’ ankle injury was not as severe as initially feared, but the tight end’s practice participation later this week will provide a clearer indication of his availability against Denver. – Myers pointed to two extended-play Seahawks touchdowns as 14 points the defense surrendered on scramble drills. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s unit will need to finish rushes and cover longer when quarterbacks escape the initial pocket. picks.headline: NFL Week 11 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Jaguars blow past Giants, Vikings stay hot with Kirk
picks.blurb: NFL Week 11 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Jaguars blow past Giants, Vikings stay hot with Kirk Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact FanSided Network Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites I'm not going to lie to you, NFL Week 11 isn't exactly loaded with marquee matchups. Teams like the Chicago Bears , Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos — you know, the contenders in this league right now — are all matched up with teams well out of the playoff race. Throw in the fact that six teams are on bye, and the schedule gets leaner. But we do have two big-time matchups with the Jacksonville Jaguars visiting the New York Giants and then a huge Sunday Night Football showdown in Mexico City with the Minnesota Vikings taking on the San Francisco 49ers for NFC supremacy. But regardless of the quality of matchup, we have every game covered in our NFL picks and predictions. We're coming off of two winning weeks in a row and are getting our mojo back. Surely a week in which there are numerous double-digit spreads with heavy and deserved favorites won't come back to haunt us. But here we go, once again delivering with NFL picks for Week 11 with predictions for every game straight-up and against the spread. NFL Week 11 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington, quarterback Trevor Lawrence | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 11 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Colts vs. Texans (TNF) Saints vs. Bears Ravens vs. Panthers Panthers -2.5 Dolphins vs. Bills Titans vs. Cowboys Cardinals vs. Chiefs Buccaneers vs. Lions Buccaneers +6.5 Steelers vs. Eagles Steelers -4.5 Jets vs. Chargers Raiders vs. Broncos Jaguars vs. Giants Vikings vs. 49ers (SNF) Bengals vs. Commanders 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 95-57 (Last week 11-3) | ATS Record: 71-78-3 (Last week 9-5) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 11 prediction to make Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Point blank, these are two of the three best teams in the NFC right now. So you throw in the fact that this game is at a neutral site in primetime and it makes it even more difficult. Looking at these two teams, though, people are going to look at the 49ers and their high-powered offense and be intrigued by that. But the Vikings have proven that, under Brian Flores, they're capable of slowing down anyone. Heck, the Lions and Packers both found that out — even if the Detroit got the win thanks to Kyler Murray. But now Kirk Cousins is back in the fold for Minnesota and we've seen him already step in and raise the baseline of the Vikings offense substantially. Who knew getting Justin Jefferson the ball was the smart play? It's that end of the field that ended up being my deciding factor here, though. The fact that the Vikings offense has found this new level of competency complements the defense so incredibly well. Moreover, the 49ers defense, though talented, hasn't exactly been infallible of late. So in Mexico City, give me the Vikings staying hot and establishing a foothold in the NFC. Easiest NFL Week 11 pick on the board Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III, quarterback Caleb Williams | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) This feels scarily too easy. Like, have oddsmakers watched the Saints recently? This defense is struggling mightily right now and the offense isn't exactly lighting the world on fire anymore either. To add to that, the Bears have been clinical more often than not this season (the last time out against the Buccaneers where Caleb Williams couldn't stop throwing picks, notwithstanding). Now we get Ben Johnson and this team coming out of a bye where they've had time to gameplan and get healthier. Yeah, that's all lining up pretty heavily toward Chicago for me, especially with this game being played in the Windy City. It's not that I think this game will end up being just a mauling on the Bears' part (though that's also not out of the question). The Saints should be able to score a bit. But it feels like Chicago will just have more consistent and perhaps unstopped success that will ultimately allow them to pull away handily. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Yes, I'm aware that Baker Mayfield's health is (once again) in question coming into this game. That's not me saying I have full faith in Jalon Daniels getting back into the offense, though he didn't play that poorly when he had to step in earlier in the season. What I think people are overlooking in this matchup is the fact that the Lions are coming off of the win in Munich and now have to travel back across the country and not get a bye week between games. That has happened for eight teams this season, traveling back from Europe and playing again in one week, and those teams are 2-5-1 straight-up, much less against the spread favored by more than a touchdowns. When you then factor in losing Aidan Hutchinson last week and what that could mean for Detroit's defense — which I wasn't exactly over the moon about to begin with — there's a path here for the Bucs to keep this close. I'll still take the Lions to win straight-up, mainly because I'm a coward and understand they are the substantially better team in this matchup. However, I do think the Buccaneers keep the game within a possession when we get to the end of it. Home / NFL About Pitch a Story Privacy Policy Legal Disclaimer Accessibility Statement

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars meet Sunday afternoon at MetLife Stadium in a matchup between two division leaders. New York enters at 5-3-1 and atop the NFC East, while Jacksonville is 7-2 and in first place in the AFC South. The Jaguars have won three straight and emerged as one of the league’s most complete teams, ranking fourth at 29.9 points per game while allowing only 16.0, second-best in the NFL. Trevor Lawrence has thrown for 2,284 yards and 21 touchdowns, while Parker Washington leads Jacksonville with 645 receiving yards. Led by J.J. McCarthy , the Giants have been more modest offensively averaging 22.6 points per game, but their defense ranks among the NFL’s best against the pass, allowing fewer than 200 yards per game. The Giants are trying to bounce back after a painful 24-21 home loss to the Washington Commanders last Thursday. New York twice took second-half leads and went in front 21-17 when McCarthy connected with Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard touchdown with 8:13 remaining, but Jayden Daniels answered with a 71-yard game-winning drive, capped by a 32-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds left. McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Cam Skattebo ran 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and Likely exploded for nine catches, 127 yards and a score. New York actually outgained Washington 399-340 but converted only four of 12 third downs and couldn’t protect the late lead. The Jaguars, meanwhile, are coming off one of their best offensive performances of the season, a 40-23 road victory over Tennessee. Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards, three touchdowns and one interception, becoming the eighth-youngest quarterback in NFL history to reach 20,000 career passing yards. Washington was his biggest weapon, catching seven passes for a career-high 152 yards and a touchdown, while Bhayshul Tuten added 88 rushing yards and a late touchdown. Jacksonville piled up 459 yards, controlled the ball for more than 38 minutes and converted seven of 14 third downs as it scored at least 30 points for the fourth consecutive game. The Jacksonville offense and specifically the Jags’ passing game against New York’s pass defense is the central matchup Sunday. These franchises don’t have an extensive rivalry, but their meetings have tended to be competitive: Jacksonville holds a 4-3 lead in the all-time regular-season series, with the teams alternating victories in each of their past five meetings. Their most recent matchup came on October 23, 2022, when the Giants rallied for a 23-17 victory in Jacksonville. away.blurb: Tuten's status for Sunday's game was brought into question after he missed the first two days of practice this week with foot and ankle injuries. He did, however, return to practice on Friday in a limited capacity. Paul Bretl, Jaguars Wire · Jaguars Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:11 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Will Jacksonville Jaguars' running back Bhayshul Tuten play in the team's Week 10 matchup against the Tennessee Titans? Will Jaguars ' RB Bhayshul Tuten play vs. Titans? He does not have an injury designation and will be good to go for Sunday's matchup. Bhayshul Tuten's season-long stats Tuten has seized control of the lead back role in Jacksonville, rushing for 521 yards this season at 4.3 yards per attempt with four touchdowns. He's been one of the better backs at making defenders miss with his speed, which has resulted in a number of chunk runs. In the passing game, he has 15 receptions for 181 yards with three touchdowns. Jaguars running back depth chart Along with Tuten, the Jaguars have Chris Rodriguez, who was on the injury report with a hand injury this week but will play. LeQuint Allen often sees the field on passing downs, where he excels in pass protection. Ameer Abdullah provides another option for the Jaguars if needed. away.headline: Jaguars-Titans Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Full-Go Status Puts Focus on Rushing Attack
away.blurb: The Jaguars are set to be without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III against the Titans as the Jaguars give them their bye week, while defensive end BJ Green will also be out as he works his way back from the injured reserve list. Tuten played in last week's game against the Baltimore Ravens despite not practicing that week with a foot/ankle injury, and he also sat out the first two practice days this week. He ended up getting 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown a week ago and did participate in Friday's practice as a limited participant, giving him the green light for Sunday against the Titans. The Jaguars had their third-worst rushing performance in terms of EPA/Rush during the 25-game Coen era on Thursday Night Football. Part of this had to do with execution, while another part of it had to do with a run-heavy second-half script after the Jaguars got up on the Ravens at halftime. Add in some bad weather that took the ball out of the hands of the passing game, and the Jaguars' rushing attack had the perfect storm for a regression game. As Coen said, there should be no long-term concerns. But in an AFC where the race for the No. 1 seed will be important week in and week out, and the Jaguars will need their running game to continue hitting its stride over the second-half of the season. home.headline: Kayvon Thibodeaux could return to NY Giants, says NFL insider
home.blurb: Kayvon Thibodeaux could return to NY Giants, says NFL insider - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Kayvon Thibodeaux could return to NY Giants, says NFL insider Trade rumors have swirled around the 25-year-old Thibodeaux since the Giants made edge defender Abdul Carter the No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. With Carter and Brian Burns, who is now out for the season with a torn ACL, it has seemed likely that Thibodeaux would leave the Giants for a bigger role and a bigger paycheck at the end of the season. "I think Brian Burns has helped him from the outside looking in, and I've asked people what does that mean when a guy turns his corner? Does that mean he's playing better and there is a sense of that but there's also just more of a sense of urgency," Schultz said. "This was another really high pick. I think it was a top five pick and obviously has been someone that Giants fans have wanted more out of. Kayvon Thibodeaux | Getty Images Ed Valentine · SB Nation Tue, November 17, 2026 at 1:29 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads "There is a scenario" in which free-agent-to-be edge defender Kayvon Thibodeaux returns to the New York Giants next season, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz. Schultz made that statement during an appearance Monday on the 'Valentine's Views' podcast. "I would have said no a month ago. I would have said no six weeks ago," Schultz said. "There is a real sentiment inside that building that Kayvon Thibodeaux has turned the corner. He's turned the corner emotionally, maturity." "You're starting to see it now and I do believe for the first time over the last let's call it year and a half, two years that there is a scenario in which Kayvon Thibodeaux is there, and I never would have thought that previously." Statistically, Thibodeaux is not having a great season. He does not have a sack, has just three quarterback hits, per Pro Football Focus is averaging a career-low two pressures per game, and his PFF pass rush win percentage of 9.3 is the second-lowest of his career. Yet, there is a sense that Thibodeaux does a lot of the dirty, unnoticed work that has helped the Giants' defense rank fifth in the league in yards and 11th in point allowed. Will that be enough to keep him in New York? Maybe. If the Giants can find the money. "It's really hard to pay three different dudes [at] essentially the same position the same type of money," Schultz said. "The Giants are not going to be able to pay three dudes $25-30 million dollars [at] essentially the same spot." home.blurb: Commanders-Giants Final Injury Report: Lucas Patrick Out, Treylon Burks Expected Back Despite Missed Practice Skip to main content SI.COM Lucas Patrick is out Thursday night against the New York Giants. The Commanders’ final injury report also ruled out tight end Colson Yankoff, leaving Washington to start Nick Allegretti at center in place of Patrick. Patrick entered concussion protocol during Sunday’s loss to the Rams, and rookie Matt Gulbin finished that game at center. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Tuesday that Allegretti will start against New York. Gulbin got the call Sunday because he had been taking the center reps while Allegretti worked at guard, a decision I wrote more about earlier this week . According to Washington's official website, the Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL. Allegretti will have to help set the protection against that defense with Jayden Daniels behind him. Treylon Burks missed Wednesday’s practice with the foot injury that kept him out against the Rams, but he has no game designation. Quinn said the day off was planned after Burks got work Tuesday and that the receiver was expected to be ready Thursday. Washington did not practice Monday and held a walkthrough Tuesday, so those first two participation reports were estimates. Burks’ place on the active list will be confirmed with Thursday’s inactives. Yankoff did not practice during the short week because of a knee injury. His absence reaches beyond the tight end rotation: Washington credited him with 185 special teams snaps this season. John Bates (shoulder) was full all three days, and Chig Okonkwo (hip) was full Tuesday and Wednesday. Neither has a game designation. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for this week, and the Vikings have started as a three-point underdog to the Niners. The over/under for this one has started at 46.5 points. The Vikings snapped their two-game losing streak this past Sunday at Lambeau Field, pasting the Green Bay Packers by a score of 30-10 to complete a sweep of the Border Battle for the 2026 season. The defense was dominant, sacking Jordan Love eight times and forcing three of the four turnovers committed by the Packers (the fourth came on special teams). But the big story was the Vikings' offense and the return of Kirk Cousins, whom the Vikings acquired at the trade deadline on Tuesday, arrived in Minnesota on Wednesday, and started on Sunday, making him the first player since at least 1950 to start games at quarterback for different teams in consecutive weeks. Cousins' last start for his former team, the Las Vegas Raiders, came against these same 49ers, who come into this game tied for the league's best record at 8-1. Like the Vikings, the Niners got their season off to a 6-0 start before seeing their first loss, a 29-20 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. After the bye, they came back to beat Cousins and the Raiders by a score of 38-17, and this past Sunday they had a back-and-forth battle with the Dallas Cowboys that saw them eventually emerge with a 46-40 victory at Jerryworld. Brock Purdy is on the short list of potential MVP candidates for this season, and he showed why against the Cowboys, completing 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns, two of which came on long passes to Christian McCaffrey, who had 161 receiving yards on the day. This matchup looks to be another matchup of a very strong offense facing off against Brian Flores' #1 defensive squad. Unlike what we saw when the Vikings faced the Bills on Monday Night, however, now it appears that the Vikings have the offense to actually allow their defense to have a bit of a rest and not allow them to get worn down late in the game. For the fourth consecutive week, the Vikings will go into a game as an underdog, ladies and gentlemen. What do you think about that? Let us know in the comments!

away.blurb: Minnesota Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman is expected to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol “very soon” and will likely return for Sunday night’s game against the San Francisco 49ers , coach Kevin O’Connell said Wednesday. Quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) and receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) are expected to be the only players held out of Wednesday’s practice, according to O’Connell, as the Vikings prepare their Week 11 injury report . Following thumb surgery Monday, Addison rejoined the team Wednesday and could return sooner than originally anticipated. Addison was believed to be a candidate for injured reserve, which requires a four-game absence, but O’Connell said the Vikings are keeping him on the active roster for now. Tight end T.J. Hockenson and receiver Jauan Jennings will also return to practice. Jennings, the former 49ers starter who declined a trade back to San Francisco last month, has missed two games because of a calf strain. “It’s going to be a boost to get Jauan back on the grass and hopefully have him available,” O’Connell said. “We know he’s going to be competing this week considering the opponent.” “That was really encouraging,” O’Connell said, “obviously subject to change as he gets into his rehab.” Addison worsened a pre-existing thumb issue during practice last week, forcing him to miss the Vikings’ 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers . ©2026 The Minnesota Star Tribune. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Drew Collings · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 18, 2026 at 7:10 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings made a blockbuster trade ahead of the deadline by reuniting with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. On the surface, this alleviates their need for a quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft. However, the opposite is actually true. This move gives the Vikings a golden opportunity to draft and develop their franchise guy. Cousins has already established himself as the starter in Minnesota. He had a fantastic debut with 21 completions for 207 yards, two touchdowns, and only one interception. He instantly raises their ceiling and turns them from a Super Bowl hopeful into a main contender. Still, the Vikings must have a long-term plan in mind. Even in the best-case scenario with Cousins leading them to a title, he's only playing a few years after. He's 38 years old and nearing retirement. So, it's vital that they add a potential franchise quarterback, or else they will be back in the position they just were. The 2027 NFL Draft quarterback class has potential, but is full of raw prospects. The upcoming quarterback class is interesting. It has prospects with sky-high potential; think of South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers or even Texas quarterback Arch Manning. However, a lot of them aren't ready for the NFL and need a few years to develop. This is why the Vikings must draft a quarterback this year. Cousins is an invaluable mentor to a young player and would let them sit, learning the scheme and developing their processing, before eventually taking over. They wouldn't be thrown into the fire, which countless teams have mistakenly done recently. Look at this year with the Las Vegas Raiders. They handled Fernando Mendoza brilliantly, allowing him to learn behind Cousins before trading him at the deadline and naming Mendoza as the starter. This has already paid dividends for them, as the first-overall pick had a great debut and matured into the role. It's a case study for how teams should handle rookie quarterbacks and is something the Vikings must mimic. Yes, they could wait another year. But there are countless uncertainties with quarterbacks, the NFL, and college football that they may never get a better chance. So, if they like a guy, why not invest in him? away.headline: Vikings-Packers Second Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday’s estimates. That doesn’t bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We’ll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. Let's dig into the full slate of Vikings injuries as a new week begins. Vikings who could return in Week 11 Van Ginkel left in the third quarter against the Packers with a leg injury and did not return. Losing arguably the most impactful player on defense and also the team leader in sacks would be devastating, but fortunately, head coach Kevin O'Connell provided an optimistic update on Monday. The head coach said Van Ginkel is "actually feeling pretty good... will more than likely be limited early on." That's encouraging news, and it's likely the Vikings held Van Ginkel out late in the Packers blowout for precautionary reasons. Hockenson missed the Packers game with chest and wrist issues, but O'Connell said that the tight end will "hopefully be available on Sunday." Like Hockenson, Jennings's return looks imminent after missing the past two games with a calf issue . O'Connell again said that he expects his receiver to be available for the 49ers game. Murray has been dealing with a hamstring injury that is progressing, but may hold him out for another week. "He'll ramp up his workload and progression," said O'Connell on Monday. "We'll see where he's at and whether he'll potentially be available this week. If not, it'll be in the not-too-distant future, but I'll keep you posted on that." Obviously, Murray would return to a backup role with Cousins now rostered, and until then, Carson Wentz will handle those duties. Vikings out for rest of 2026 season The Vikings lost one more player this week, adding edge Bo Richter to their list of players shut down for the season. Donovan Jackson, Josh Oliver, Jamal Adams and Tyler Batty are also out for the year. He played LG quite admirably in the preseason. He may just be their best option at the position in Fairchild can’t go. Cincinnati has been blessed with tremendous continuity along it’s o-line. His numbers also show the decline in long runs, because "last year was 12.4. They were sixth in the NFL. 2024 they were 12.7. This year it's 9.1. So, they're just not getting enough in the run game." Jacory Croskey-Merritt' s already under immediate pressure to fix a worrying problem for the Washington Commanders , even though the second-year running back has only just returned to the field. It's runs of 10 yards or more, gains JCM specialized in creating during a breakout rookie campaign . In fact, "12 percent of his carries were for 10 or more yards. This year, only six percent of his carries have been for 10 or more yards," according to ESPN's John Keim , speaking on The John Keim Report . Croskey-Merritt's time on the treatment table has disrupted his rhythm this season, but he's not the only back struggling to produce explosive plays for the Commanders. Fortunately, a subtle change made by offensive coordinator David Blough could help boost the numbers for every member of Washington's rushing attack. Croskey-Merritt returning to the dynamic, award-winning form he showed as a rookie would improve this season's middling number. He's still a nifty, one-cut-and-go runner who can get to the second level in a hurry and accelerate in the open field. ‘Bill' has five runs of 20-plus yards , including two of 40 or more, since entering the pros. He also averaged 2.1 yards after contact per rushing attempt during his maiden campaign, according to Pro Football Reference . Washington's offense is missing those numbers and qualities, even after the team reunited with two scheme-appropriate running backs. Patrick entered concussion protocol during Sunday’s loss to the Rams, and rookie Matt Gulbin finished that game at center. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Tuesday that Allegretti will start against New York. Gulbin got the call Sunday because he had been taking the center reps while Allegretti worked at guard, a decision I wrote more about earlier this week . According to Washington's official website, the Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL. Allegretti will have to help set the protection against that defense with Jayden Daniels behind him. Treylon Burks missed Wednesday’s practice with the foot injury that kept him out against the Rams, but he has no game designation. Quinn said the day off was planned after Burks got work Tuesday and that the receiver was expected to be ready Thursday. home.blurb: The Giants also expect starting quarterback J.J. McCarthy to be available despite the painful hip pointer he suffered against the Eagles. Ar’Darius Washington — The veteran safety had what could have been a game-sealing interception of Jayden Daniels at the Washington 46-yard line with 2:15 to play. The offense could not close the game out, however, and the Commanders took advantage of their final opportunity. In his best game as a Giant, Washington also had six tackles and two passes defensed. Linebacker Malik Harrison, questionable with a groin injury, is the only member of the New York Giants carrying an injury designation heading into Thursday’s game with the Washington Commanders. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy (hip), and running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) will play as the 5-2-1 Giants seek to solidify their NFC East lead. It will be interesting to see if McCarthy’s mobility is limited. Andrew: It’s funny, because the Giants fumbled away a chance at the win in overtime when they could have made a field goal to win, yet all the media scrutiny seemed to be on the Commanders... However, I’d agree that the decision making around the very last play drew lots of justified criticism on both the Commanders coaching and Jayden Daniels for not having better situational awareness. It was followed up with a similar end-of-game play against the 49ers the very next week that drew criticism of both the coaches and Jayden Daniels. I think that double whammy got people looking at everything a bit more closely, but it’s really just been a litany of questionable decisions (mostly with the coaching and offensive playcalling) over multiple games that has Commanders fans unhappy with their play on the field. Most of the scrutiny has been on OC David Blough, who skipped a few grade levels going from Assistant QB Coach to OC when maybe he needed more time to learn his craft. I honestly put that more on Dan Quinn for promoting him too quickly though, I wouldn’t expect anyone to do well with that big of a promotion. Skattebo was held out of Sunday’s division game against the Philadelphia Eagles because of his hamstring injury. That was at Lincoln Financial Field, the place where he dislocated his ankle a season ago. Thursday’s game will be in the national spotlight, and we know Skattebo loves that. “He was very close,” Harbaugh said on Monday morning. “We just decided to not take the risk that would go with it. There were some things that he was going to be limited just a bit, maybe. We decided not to go down that road because of the short week this week.
